feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: Candidates vying for Nebraska House seat face off in debate
entry.summary: The candidates in a competitive U.S. House race in Nebraska faced off in a debate. The winner would replace retiring GOP Rep. Don Bacon.

entry.title: Trump continues to rally voters in red states as Republicans face competitive races
entry.summary: How does President Trump's travel compare to past campaigns and what does it say about Republicans' level of concern about the midterms?

entry.title: What the GOP's money moves suggest about the party's midterm outlook
entry.summary: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with political analyst Ron Brownstein about recent shifts in GOP spending and messaging, and what they suggest about how the party views its chances in the midterms.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: Trump's campaign tour continues as Republicans rally voters ahead of midterms, Ukraine faces limited access to Starshield technology, Houthi rebels hit Saudi oil company building.

entry.title: LA fire survivors face another setback with FEMA program delays
entry.summary: The fight over a FEMA program aiding some of LA's most vulnerable wildfire victims is the latest setback for hundreds of fire survivors who still haven't rebuilt after the deadly 2025 infernos.

entry.title: Group that plants fruit trees in vacant lots grows to cities nationwide
entry.summary: A Kansas City group set up to help volunteers plant fruit trees in vacant city lots has quickly branched out across the country with almost 850 orchards in 17 cities with more to come.

entry.title: Despite bad inflation report, Trump says economy is doing fine
entry.summary: The latest tough inflation report reinforces the challenge for President Trump and GOP candidates ahead into the midterm elections.

entry.title: Social Security could soon run out of money. Here are some possible solutions
entry.summary: Social Security may run short of money to make full payments to retirees as soon as 2032. The team from NPR's Planet Money examines possible solutions.

entry.title: Wyoming tribes ask church pastor to leave after viral sermon
entry.summary: Tribes on the Wind River Reservation in Wyoming are asking a Christian pastor to leave after she denigrated their native religion in a sermon.

entry.title: France investigates cyberattack that hacked retailers' refrigeration systems
entry.summary: France has opened an investigation into a cyberattack that hit hundreds of food retailers, causing refrigerators to malfunction across the country.
